institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The most important aspect was that Sciences Po offered courses that were able to replace my mandatory courses (Dansk og komparativ politik 3 and Europæisk politik). Another crucial aspect was that Sciences Po is the third best university in the world for politics (following Harvard and Oxford).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy! The staff in the reception does not speak English but just check your email or ask other students if you need help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much. You can sign up for a 'buddy' (and be paired with another Sciences Po student) but I chose not to. I also did not sign up for the introduction week because you had to pay to attend. There were some free activities (such as tours of the campus and library, presentations of student clubs/associations, etc.) but I had covid that week and did not go. Therefore, I had to just show up for my lessons the following week without knowing my way around campus but I asked random students for directions and everything worked out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Finding a place to live in Paris for only a few months is difficult. The first place I lived in was disgusting and my parents wanted me to move out immediately because they did not think it was safe enough for me to live there. I then got a temporary room in the Danish House in Cité internationale universitaire de Paris that I could only stay in for about a month. I ended up renting an AirBnB afterwards which was really expensive. 

I recommend finding an agent before moving to Paris as those of my friends who had done that lived in really nice places. Apparently, you pay a fee for them to help you but I definitely think that it's worth it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Rent is much higher and quality is much lower compared to Copenhagen.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
You register online about a month before the semester starts. I was in Chicago and the time difference meant that I had to get up really early, as it is first come first serve and you have to be ready when registration opens. A lot of courses filled immediately and my screen froze multiple times. I had a lot of technical issues and it was very stressful! All the error codes were written in French, and overall, it was just not a good experience at all. 

If this happens to you, take screen shots so you can prove that you had technical issues.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I emailed IT multiple times. They replied quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
At first I could not get the courses that I needed for Europæisk politik at home as they had all filled up in a matter of minutes. I recommend waiting around for a little while if this happens to you because eventually a spot opened up for one of the courses I needed and I quickly registered for that one.

I still needed one more mandatory course, and I chose to register for a random course that had 'Europe' in the title. It had not been pre-approved by my home university so it was very risky but I did not have any other options. I immediately sent an application to KU but they spent more than the promised five or six weeks to approve the course. I called and emailed KU multiple times and had to attend my first lesson of the course without knowing whether it had been approved. Eventually, however, it worked out and they approved the course. 

As for my elective courses, the two that I had wanted to take and that had already been approved by KU were either full or removed from this year's course list. Therefore, I ended up choosing two random courses that seemed somewhat interesting and did not clash with my other lessons. They were eventually approved without any issues (but only after the semester had started because KU was so slooooooow).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get as many courses pre approved as possible. Don't just apply for the minimum amount of courses that you need because you may not be able to register for them and in that case it is good to have some backup options.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The teaching was definitely less research based compared to KU. There were nearly no readings and I only had one lecture a week. The others were seminars where you're expected to actively participate and sometimes make presentations. Overall, Sciences Po was more practical and less theoretical compared to KU. The final exams did not draw on the readings but rather on what your teacher had told you in class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It felt more like high school than university. There are lots of small assignments such as presentations and creative writing exercises. In some classes you are also graded based on your participation. All of these assignments weigh differently and contribute to your final grade. We also had a lot of multiple choice exams. Most exams were pen and paper and closed book. The advantage is that it is easier to predict what grade you end up with and that it is a more active learning style. The disadvantage is that it feels less academic.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Nation and nationalism: several approaches to basic concepts (5 ECTS - elective)
Technology, war and politics (5 ECTS - elective - do not recommend)
EU integration and its challenges (5 ECTS - Europæisk politik)
Social policies in Europe (5 ECTS - Europæisk politik - highly recommend) 
Comparative politics (10 ECTS - Dansk og komparativ politik 3)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Social policies in Europe. The professor is highly knowledgable and great at drawing comparisons between different welfare models. The course is very historical and one of the more academic ones I took.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't recall any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Housing was really expensive. 
There were no books which was unexpected so no expenses there. 
You can definitely spend less money on food, I just really liked going out to eat at really amazing French restaurants.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had some sport clubs but you needed a doctor's notice (even for yoga) so I did not participate

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I did not participate in any. 
Paris is such a great city so my activities consisted of going on long walks and visiting museums (most of them are free), bars and restaurants. I was really busy with that so I did not need to sign up for anything via Sciences Po.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See above. Please just take advantage of the fact that you'll be living in one of the best cities in the world. There are endless things to see and do

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Some people say they don't speak English but if you're patient and creative you'll be able to communicate just fine.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I exclusively hung out with other international exchange students. I really enjoyed that because I love being part of international communities.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The French are rude. There is not much you can do about it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food, art and wine

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. The university is fine although not super academic
2. Going on exchange (anywhere) is amazing and I highly recommend doing so 
3. Make sure to have a lot of potential courses pre-approved

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My social life. I met so many wonderful people from all over the world. Everyone is very open and quite spontaneous as they do not really have many other responsibilities. Everyone is very keen on making friends and having a good experience studying abroad.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Being ill. I sadly had to deal with a lot of illness which was exhausting and quite lonely (especially in the beginning). 
2. Housing. Moving twice was hard

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
